societies.name: Steel Beach — Luna under the Central Computer
societies.society: Computer-governed lunar provision before the later crisis

scope.continuity: Steel Beach novel-specific Eight Worlds variant
scope.period: Established Central Computer support before the later raids and acute malfunction
scope.population: Living human and active human-derived lunar citizens
exclusions: Every Eight Worlds novel as an identical timeline
Inactive personality recordings as supported active residents

societies.description:
Luna’s Central Computer maintains the society in which oxygen, food, water and medical intervention are routinely provided. The setting separates material support from a person’s immediate success at paid employment, while still supplying jobs and occasions for purposeful activity. Guarantees are rated strong within the established order, with qualifications about coercive intervention and the later computer crisis. A life-support floor is not an assertion that every personal preference is respected.

The Computer is government, court, information source and intimate adviser, placing authority near autonomous AI control. Human occupations and preferences do not establish a right to overrule that system. Journalism, ranching, care and recreational construction can all be useful work, so the comfortable economy provides no reliable nonworking census. The point concerns this novel’s implemented Luna rather than importing its institutions backward into every Eight Worlds story. Active human-derived people are an explicit proxy where relevant; stored recordings and the hidden surface community are outside this provision scope.

guarantees.basis: The review explicitly lists society-provided oxygen, food, water and medical care; the setting reference identifies the controlling machine system.

control.basis: The Central Computer governs and adjudicates ordinary life; its assistance is not human collective ownership.

nonworking.basis: No all-person useful-work census; voluntary creation, care, maintenance and research remain work.

societies.society: Ordinary citizens under nanotechnological Aristoi rule

scope.period: Established reconstructed Logarchy before the secret-world conflict
scope.population: Living human Demos in functioning Logarchy domains
exclusions: Each daimone as an extra independent citizen

societies.description:
The Logarchy’s nanotechnology supports a comfortable ordinary population with serious illnesses eliminated and injuries repairable. The author explicitly frames the setting as post-scarcity, while the detailed reference connects its productive capabilities to a specialized ruling class. Guarantees receive a strong but qualified estimate within the established domains: routine material ease and healing are clear, while individual rulers can shape local conditions and residents do not possess the same powers.

Only the Aristoi are authorized to develop and use the decisive nanotechnology. They govern their domains, making control highly concentrated in human and human-derived elites rather than common ownership or external AI sovereignty. Competitive examinations permit movement within the hierarchy but do not grant everyone equal authority over production. The rulers’ divided mental subselves are not multiplied into a population of independent nonworkers. Ordinary and elite residents can still create, study, govern and care for others; post-scarcity alone does not establish that no useful work remains, so participation stays unresolved.

societies.name: Implied Spaces — The supported constructed-world civilization
societies.society: The established human communities supported by pocket-universe infrastructure

scope.continuity: Walter Jon Williams’s original novel setting
scope.period: Established civilization before Vindex’s resurrection sabotage and war
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived residents of functioning constructed worlds
exclusions: Deliberately chosen fantasy scarcity as universal deprivation
Every pocket universe as having identical local government

societies.description:
Constructed pocket universes and their sustaining supercomputers provide the setting for a civilization explicitly described by the gathered reader account as post-scarcity. Designer embodiment, resurrection and the ability to inhabit elaborately built worlds are implemented features, not merely a proposal to upload someday. Guarantees are provisionally favorable for functioning communities, with a broad allowance for unequal local arrangements and vulnerability of the underlying infrastructure. Chosen fantasy-world hardship is not assigned to all residents.

Control remains unresolved. Human political institutions coexist with indispensable supercomputers, and infrastructure dependence alone does not prove that those machines are independent sovereigns. The later corruption and resurrection attacks demonstrate an important failure mode, but are outside the earlier support score. Humans and active human-derived residents form the explicit population proxy; backups are excluded. Exploration, art, research and infrastructure work continue, so neither extended life nor constructed worlds supplies a nonworking percentage. Publisher and plot context support the mechanism while the post-scarcity interpretation remains honestly labeled as secondary.

societies.name: Riding the Torch — The abundant refugee convoy
societies.society: The matter-energy supplied human torchship population

scope.continuity: Norman Spinrad’s novella as described in the bounded reader plot account
scope.period: Established centuries-long convoy life before the scout revelation
scope.population: Living human inhabitants of the refugee torchship convoy
exclusions: The Council’s navigation powers as proof of ownership of every personal fabricator
Artists and pilots as doing no useful work
A collective search for a planet as present material starvation

societies.description:
The refugee convoy can manipulate matter and energy to shape living environments, meals and experiences while traveling between stars. Most residents enjoy a continuing culture of sensory art, parties and leisure rather than earning ordinary subsistence through production jobs. Guarantees receive a favorable estimate for that functioning technological support. The evidence is a clearly labeled reader plot account, so enforceable civic rights and the exact limits of provision remain uncertain.

A Council of Pilots coordinates the search for a habitable destination, while individuals can reshape their own surroundings. Navigation authority does not by itself establish centralized ownership of production, nor does personal access prove equal command of the entire infrastructure; control stays unresolved. A high, broad nonworking estimate follows the extensive leisure description, with substantial room for pilots, artists, care, maintenance and useful creative work. It is not a canonical census. The failure to find a new home is not confused with immediate inability to provide necessities aboard the existing convoy.

guarantees.basis: The specific plot review describes actual matter-energy manipulation, food/experience creation and continuing leisure for most convoy residents.

control.basis: Council navigation and individual environmental creation do not establish one effective productive-ownership model.

nonworking.basis: Extensive leisure supports .75 [.35,.95] as a broad editorial estimate; artists, pilots and other useful contributors still count.

review_notes: Twelve additional ordered short checks yield four provisional societies; the goal remains active below 500.
Steel Beach’s concrete oxygen/food/care is verified without importing it into every Eight Worlds novel. Useful journalism and ranching remain work.
Aristoi rulers are human-derived elites; daimones are not multiplied into a false human denominator.
Implied Spaces infrastructure is not declared mere simulation or sovereign AI by default; informal post-scarcity interpretation is labeled.
Riding the Torch’s material technology is explicit in a specific reader account; artists and pilots remain useful contributors.
Triton has a clear access floor but an unresolved automation link. Neither an attractive social constitution nor computer accounting alone secures admission.
Unrelated real agriculture, political-economy essays, government manufacture and educational results were discarded. No full fiction reconstruction was undertaken.
